request: how does a matrix act on a vector, column by column?

beats.intent: The grid with i-hat, j-hat and a vector v at (1, 2)
beats.narration: Here is a vector v at one, two: one step along i-hat and two steps along j-hat.
beats.code:
stage.title("A matrix times a vector")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left", y_extent=4)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 2), label="v")
stage.caption("v = 1 i-hat + 2 j-hat")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The grid moving so i-hat lands on (2, 1) and j-hat on (-1, 1)
beats.narration: Apply the matrix with columns two, one and minus one, one. The basis vectors land on those columns, and v rides along.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[2, -1], [1, 1]], riders=[i_hat, j_hat, v])
stage.caption("i-hat goes to column 1, j-hat to column 2")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: One copy of column one, then two copies of column two, tip to tail, ending at (0, 3)
beats.narration: So v lands on one copy of the first column plus two copies of the second: that walk ends at zero, three.
beats.code:
p2 = draw_plane(stage, where="left", y_extent=4)
c1 = draw_vector(stage, p2, (2, 1), color=GREEN)
s1 = draw_arrow(stage, p2.c2p(2, 1), p2.c2p(1, 2), color=RED)
s2 = draw_arrow(stage, p2.c2p(1, 2), p2.c2p(0, 3), color=RED)
mv = draw_vector(stage, p2, (0, 3), color=YELLOW, label="Mv")
stage.caption("1 of column one, then 2 of column two")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The product written as a combination of the columns
beats.narration: Written out: the matrix times one, two is one times the first column plus two times the second.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}",
               r"= 1\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + 2\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}",
               where="right")
stage.caption("The entries of v weight the columns")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: if a matrix stretches the plane why does area get multiplied by the determinant

beats.intent: The unit square shaded on the grid
beats.narration: Start with the unit square: one by one, area one.
beats.code:
stage.title("Area and the determinant")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
sq = draw_unit_square(stage, p)
stage.caption("The unit square has area 1")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The grid stretched three times wider and twice as tall, the square becoming a 3 by 2 box
beats.narration: Now stretch x by three and y by two. The square becomes a rectangle three wide and two tall.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[3, 0], [0, 2]], riders=[sq])
stage.label(sq, "area 6", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("3 wide times 2 tall: area 6")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: A small triangle on the grid growing by the same factor
beats.narration: It is not just squares. A triangle of area one half is stretched the same way and ends up with area three.
beats.code:
p2 = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
tri = Polygon(p2.c2p(0, 0), p2.c2p(1, 0), p2.c2p(0, 1), color=TEAL, fill_opacity=0.5)
stage.play(FadeIn(tri))
apply_matrix(stage, p2, [[3, 0], [0, 2]], riders=[tri])
stage.label(tri, "area 3", direction=UP, color=TEAL)
stage.caption("Area 1/2 becomes 3: also times 6")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The determinant of the stretch computed beside the picture
beats.narration: Every area is multiplied by the same number, and that number is the determinant: three times two minus zero.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\det\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = 3 \cdot 2 - 0 \cdot 0",
               r"\det\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = 6", where="right")
stage.caption("Every area is multiplied by the determinant")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: what are the eigenvectors of a reflection?

beats.intent: A vector v above the mirror line along the x-axis
beats.narration: Take the reflection across the x-axis, and a vector v at two, one.
beats.code:
stage.title("Eigenvectors of a reflection")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
mirror = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(-4, 0), p.c2p(4, 0), color=BLUE)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 1), label="v")
stage.caption("Reflect the plane across the x-axis")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The plane flipping over, v landing at (2, -1) off its own line
beats.narration: Flip the plane over the mirror. v lands at two, minus one, pointing a different way, so it is not an eigenvector.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[1, 0], [0, -1]], riders=[v])
stage.caption("v changes direction: not an eigenvector")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: Arrows along the mirror stay put, arrows across it flip on their own line
beats.narration: A vector lying on the mirror does not move at all. A vector straight across it flips, but stays on its line. Only the red one is knocked off.
beats.code:
p2 = draw_plane(stage, where="left", x_extent=2, y_extent=2)
eig = show_eigenvectors(stage, p2, [[1, 0], [0, -1]])
stage.caption("Yellow arrows stay on their lines")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: A mirror along y = x: arrows on the diagonal stay, arrows across it flip
beats.narration: The same happens for any mirror. Reflect across the line y equals x: the diagonal one, one stays, and one, minus one flips.
beats.code:
p3 = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
d1 = draw_span(stage, p3, (1, 1), color=YELLOW)
d2 = draw_span(stage, p3, (1, -1), color=TEAL)
a = draw_vector(stage, p3, (1.5, 1.5), color=YELLOW)
b = draw_vector(stage, p3, (1, -1), color=TEAL)
apply_matrix(stage, p3, [[0, 1], [1, 0]], riders=[a, b])
stage.caption("Mirror y = x: same story on the diagonals")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The two eigenvalues of any reflection
beats.narration: So every reflection has two eigen-directions: along the mirror with eigenvalue one, and across it with eigenvalue minus one.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\text{along the mirror: } \lambda = 1", r"\text{along: } \lambda = 1, \quad \text{across: } \lambda = -1", where="right")
stage.caption("Eigenvalues 1 and -1")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: what does a linear transformation do to a circle

beats.intent: The unit circle with two radii along the diagonals
beats.narration: Draw the unit circle, with two radii pointing along the diagonals.
beats.code:
stage.title("Circles become ellipses")
p = draw_plane(stage, where="left")
r1 = np.linalg.norm(p.c2p(1, 0) - p.c2p(0, 0))
ring = Circle(radius=r1, color=TEAL, stroke_width=5).move_to(p.c2p(0, 0))
stage.play(Create(ring))
a = draw_vector(stage, p, (0.71, 0.71), color=YELLOW)
b = draw_vector(stage, p, (0.71, -0.71), color=RED)
stage.caption("A circle of radius 1")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The grid moving by the matrix, the circle stretching into an ellipse
beats.narration: Apply the matrix two, one, one, two. The grid tilts and stretches, and the circle becomes an ellipse.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[2, 1], [1, 2]], riders=[ring, a, b])
stage.caption("The circle is now an ellipse")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The two radii after the move: one three times longer, one unchanged
beats.narration: Follow the radii. The yellow one is stretched to length three, the red one keeps length one. They are the long and short axes of the ellipse.
beats.code:
stage.label(a, "length 3", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(b, "length 1", direction=DOWN, color=RED)
highlight(stage, ring)
stage.caption("Long axis 3, short axis 1")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The ellipse's area compared with the determinant
beats.narration: The circle had area pi. The ellipse has area pi times three times one, and three is exactly the determinant.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\text{area}: \pi \to \pi \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 3\pi", r"\text{area} \times 3, \quad \det = 4 - 1 = 3", where="right")
stage.caption("The area grows by the determinant")
stage.pause(1.5)

stage.caption("f' = 0 exactly where f is flat")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.narration: Between them f' is negative, and that is exactly where f goes downhill.

request: how can lots of waves add up to one single pulse

beats.intent: Three moving waves and their white sum
beats.narration: When waves overlap, their heights simply add. Here are three waves and, in white, their sum.

stage.title("Superposition")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-4, 4), y_range=(-2, 2))
w = superpose_waves(stage, ax, [(0.6, 1, 1), (0.6, 2, 2), (0.6, 3, 3)], t_end=3)
stage.caption("Add the heights point by point")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: Five cosine waves of rising frequency, all peaking together at 0
beats.narration: Now line up five cosines, of frequency one to five, so that they all peak at zero.
beats.code:
stage.clear(keep=[ax])
cols = [BLUE, TEAL, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE]
waves = VGroup(*[ax.plot(lambda x, k=k: np.cos(k * x), x_range=[-4, 4, 0.02], color=c, stroke_opacity=0.7)
                 for k, c in zip(range(1, 6), cols)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(c) for c in waves], lag_ratio=0.3), run_time=2.5)
stage.caption("They agree at 0 and disagree elsewhere")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: Their average: a peak at 0 and small ripples elsewhere
beats.narration: Average them. At zero they all agree and pile up; everywhere else they partly cancel.
beats.code:
avg = lambda n: (lambda x: sum(np.cos(k * x) for k in range(1, n + 1)) / n)
s = ax.plot(avg(5), x_range=[-4, 4, 0.01], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(FadeOut(waves), Create(s), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("Five waves: a bump at 0")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: More and more waves: the bump sharpening into a thin pulse
beats.narration: Use ten waves, then twenty, then thirty. The bump gets narrower and the ripples die down: a single sharp pulse.
beats.code:
for n in (10, 20, 30):
    stage.play(Transform(s, ax.plot(avg(n), x_range=[-4, 4, 0.005], color=WHITE, stroke_width=5)), run_time=1.2)
stage.equation(r"\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n} \cos(kx)", where="right")
stage.caption("Thirty waves: one sharp pulse")
stage.pause(1.5)

request: how does data flow through a neural network with three layers

beats.intent: Three columns of neurons, 3 inputs, 4 hidden and 2 outputs, joined by weights
beats.narration: A small network: three inputs on the left, four hidden neurons in the middle, two outputs on the right. Every line is a weight.
beats.code:
stage.title("Data flowing through a network")
net = draw_neural_net(stage, layers=(3, 4, 2), pulse_through=False)
stage.label(net.layers[0], "input", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(net.layers[1], "hidden", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(net.layers[2], "output", direction=DOWN)
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The inputs lighting up and signals running along every weight to the hidden layer
beats.narration: The inputs light up, and their values run along every weight into the hidden layer. Each hidden neuron adds up what reaches it.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[n.animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.9) for n in net.layers[0]])
e1 = net.edges[:12]
sparks = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.07, color=YELLOW).move_to(e.get_start()) for e in e1])
stage.add(sparks)
stage.play(*[MoveAlongPath(s, e) for s, e in zip(sparks, e1)], run_time=1.5)
stage.play(FadeOut(sparks), *[n.animate.set_fill(TEAL, opacity=0.8) for n in net.layers[1]])
stage.caption("Each hidden neuron sums its weighted inputs")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: Signals moving on from the hidden layer to the two outputs
beats.narration: Then the hidden layer passes its values on, along its own weights, to the two outputs.
beats.code:
e2 = net.edges[12:]
sparks2 = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.07, color=TEAL).move_to(e.get_start()) for e in e2])
stage.add(sparks2)
stage.play(*[MoveAlongPath(s, e) for s, e in zip(sparks2, e2)], run_time=1.5)
stage.play(FadeOut(sparks2), *[n.animate.set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.9) for n in net.layers[2]])
stage.caption("Outputs are built from the hidden layer")
stage.pause(1.5)

beats.intent: The two steps written as formulas
beats.narration: Each step is a weighted sum plus a bias, passed through a squashing function: input to hidden, hidden to output.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"h = \sigma(W_1 x + b_1)", r"h = \sigma(W_1 x + b_1) \\ y = \sigma(W_2 h + b_2)", where="right")
stage.caption("Always left to right: input, hidden, output")
stage.pause(1.5)
